citation: Borkowski, Jarema, Kladz & Smoliar (2026). Temporally Qualified Building Elements. Technologies 14(7):413. [FULL_TEXT_READ -- see file 07; Zotero duplicate item JSYCVGH9/attachment CVGD2BLV owns the PDF, item NQ3KGDWN is a metadata-only duplicate]
identity_mechanism: NEW persistent URI identifier (e.g. bph:wall-W01) minted for an OWL instance of BuildingElement (subclass of DOLCE:PhysicalEndurant), independent of IFC GUID; the IFC GUID is demoted to a phase-level backlink attribute (hasIFCGuid) used only to trace back to the source IFC file, not as the identity anchor
identity_persistence: YES (conceptually and empirically demonstrated via a small, manually-instantiated case study: 3 elements x 3 Revit/IFC phase-files, validated with HermiT reasoner + 8/8 competency questions answered correctly; explicit self-acknowledged limitation: cross-phase identity MATCHING itself is manual/expert-judgement, not automated or deterministically validated)
model_version_context: YES -- 3 separate Revit files (.rvt), one per phase (Design/As-Built/FM), each exported to its own IFC file via Revit 2026.2; phases ordered by a transitive precedes relation (a genuine previous/next-revision chain, used to answer CQ8); each phase bound to its specific source IFC file/GUID via hasIFCGuid (a specific model-snapshot binding). No file hash, no explicit version-number scheme, no CDE/ISO19650-revision concept.
provenance_source: PARTIAL -- source-file backtracking only, via the hasIFCGuid attribute on each reified phase-relation instance (records which source GUID/file a phase-state came from); no assertion-timestamp, no record of who/what entered a value (instances were manually entered)
provenance_measurement: NOT_APPLICABLE (no sensor/measurement content in this paper)
provenance_processing: NOT_REPORTED (no processing-provenance property; values manually transcribed from Revit/IFC with no recorded transformation metadata)
human_accountability: NOT_REPORTED (no human-actor property anywhere in the 9-class schema or the event-layer extension; PhaseTransitionEvent records only source-phase/target-phase/affected-element, not who/what performed the transition)
reviewer_approver: NOT_REPORTED (no reviewer/approver concept; a 'technical inspection' is named narratively as the trigger for one material-constitution change, but is not modeled as a distinct, accountable record)
validity_scope_evidence: Confirmed absent via full-text read: no valid_from/valid_to bound, no operating-condition/protocol/configuration-applicability concept, no explicit supersession-of-EVIDENCE rule anywhere in 26 pages. The phase-ordering (precedes) and disjoint DesignPhase/AsBuiltPhase/FacilityManagementPhase subclasses are a MODEL_VERSION_CONTEXT mechanism (which phase/file a value belongs to), explicitly NOT an evidence-validity/applicability rule about when/under-what-conditions a value is trustworthy or reusable -- these are kept distinct per this correction pass's definition.
forward_traceability: PARTIAL -- CQ1-CQ8 (Table 3) support forward querying of an element's own property/state history across ITS OWN phases (e.g. 'which elements changed material between design and as-built'), but do not traverse a Sensor->Evidence->Inspection-record chain
reverse_traceability: PARTIAL -- same basis; reverse navigation (isPhaseOf, phase-to-endurant) is structurally supported but not demonstrated for cross-system/cross-record use
integrity_rules: YES -- 6 OWL 2 DL axioms (BuildingElement has >=1 phase; PhaseQualifiedRelation has exactly 1 element + 1 phase; BuildingElement/LifecyclePhase disjoint; precedes transitive; phase subclasses pairwise disjoint; hasPhase = inverse isPhaseOf), all validated via HermiT reasoner with zero contradictions on the case-study graph
shacl_or_equivalent: NO -- OWL 2 DL + HermiT reasoner (description-logic consistency checking), not SHACL; a different validation family (open-world DL reasoning vs. closed-world SHACL constraint validation)
invalid_link_tests: PARTIAL -- exactly ONE deliberate negative test was performed, and it is at the ONTOLOGY-SCHEMA level (an individual was intentionally given dual BuildingElement/LifecyclePhase classification to test the disjointness axiom; HermiT correctly flagged the ontology inconsistent), NOT at the identity-mapping/data-instance level; the full Q5 taxonomy (duplicate/orphan/wrong/stale/conflicting-mapping GUID) was NOT tested anywhere in the paper
validation_method: YES, multi-part and confirmed: (1) HermiT reasoner consistency + cardinality validation; (2) one deliberate schema-axiom violation test; (3) real 3-file Revit/IFC case study (1 building, 3 elements, 3 phases, 27 reification instances); (4) 8/8 competency questions answered correctly via SPARQL, each formally mapped (Table 3) to the exact classes/relations/axioms required; (5) full reproducibility via a published open-research-data repository (Turtle ontology + instances + SPARQL queries, DOI 10.71724/be6h-n995). Identity-MATCHING accuracy itself was NOT measured (performed by manual expert judgement).
already_established: CONFIRMED (full text): the IFC-GUID-fragmentation-across-life-cycle-phase-files problem is explicitly named, diagrammed, and solved via a working (small-scale, manually-instantiated) DOLCE-grounded persistent-identity mechanism, validated by a reasoner and 8 competency questions; the paper explicitly claims priority ('to our knowledge, the first construction ontology that grounds element identity across lifecycle phases in a foundational ontology'); the paper explicitly states (Discussion) that this identity layer is intended as 'the semantic anchor to which... sensor readings, inspection results, and maintenance events' can refer
remaining_gap: CONFIRMED remaining gaps vs Paper 2: (1) identity MATCHING across phases is manual/expert-judgement, not automated or deterministically validated; (2) no Condition_Evidence_ID or Inspection_Record_ID as first-class, accountable entities -- crack/inspection/repair content is folded into bare property-value changes with zero accountability fields; (3) no deliberate identity-MAPPING negative/invalid-case testing (only one schema-axiom test); (4) no evidence-validity/applicability concept in the strict sense (confirmed absent, not just unconfirmed); (5) no forward/reverse traceability across a multi-record, cross-system chain -- CQs stay within one endurant's own phase history; (6) validation is single-building, 3-element, manually-instantiated, explicitly flagged by the authors as a scale/generalizability limitation; (7) no CDE/ISO19650-style model-revision governance
novelty_threat_level: HIGH (specifically and narrowly to the identity-governance/GAP-B sub-claim; explicitly NOT VERY_HIGH against Paper 2's full 8-component core contribution, since 6 of those 8 components -- evidence provenance beyond a bare source backlink, evidence validity/applicability, accountable inspection records, cross-system forward/reverse traceability, deterministic multi-hop integrity validation, and identity-mapping negative testing -- are confirmed absent from this paper)
paper2_implication: Paper 2 CANNOT claim novelty for: naming GUID fragmentation across life-cycle-phase files as a gap; proposing a persistent, GUID-independent identifier for a BIM component that survives across phase files; or an endurant/perdurant-style separation of identity from phase-state -- all now full-text-confirmed as claimed by Borkowski (2026), including an explicit priority claim. Paper 2's defensible novelty must be built on: (a) an identity-linking step that is automatable/auditable (not manual, unlike Borkowski's); (b) integrating identity governance with first-class, accountable Condition_Evidence_ID and Inspection_Record_ID entities (absent in Borkowski); (c) deliberate identity-MAPPING negative/invalid-case testing across a cross-system chain (Borkowski tests only one schema axiom); (d) an explicit evidence-validity/applicability rule (confirmed absent in Borkowski); (e) forward/reverse traceability that crosses Sensor/Evidence/Inspection-record boundaries, not just an element's own phase history.

citation: Ciccarese, Soiland-Reyes, Belhajjame, Gray, Goble & Clark (2013). PAV ontology. J Biomed Semantics 4:37.
asset_type: digital resources/documents (biomedical semantics domain, NOT BIM)
